gitCommit.subject: Stop the mobile-web specs depending on page-one position
gitCommit.body:
Stop the mobile-web specs depending on page-one position

Both failures came from the locator, not the product: the seeded rows
they look for are dated early in the month, and every spec that creates
a transaction through the UI dates it today, so an unfiltered list buries
them as soon as anything else has run. Searching for the row instead
makes them independent of whatever is in the database.

Break-tested by pointing the search at a row that does not exist, which
fails the list assertion — so the filter is doing the work and the
assertion is not passing on an empty page.

Full suite: 92 passed, 0 failed, and 1.3 minutes quicker without the two
timeouts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
